admission.justification: The governance checks fail when a new test module is absent from the catalogs or when the measured digest disagrees with the source-derived ownership; a stale static pin would either fail the checks or hide a real ownership drift. Both catalogs realize the obligation.

applicability: The governed test-evidence catalogs of the repository and the ownership checks that read them.
conditions: The new test module appears as a consumer in the lifecycle catalog and in its lane's population.
The catalogs' ownership checks read the R51 source-derived ownership; a later change that alters the catalogs is reconciled there, not by a stored static pin.
exclusions: The superseded static digest pin and the old line position are historical observations, not current facts.
The historical repin's 19 contracts and 83 artifacts describe the catalog at the moment that pin was measured; they are not an immutable count the catalog must keep.
This obligation governs catalog registration; it does not name the test module's own behavior (rule 4a owns that).
statement: The new report-test module is registered as a consumer in both governed test-evidence catalogs, and the catalogs' ownership is the R51 owner's computed source-derived ownership: no catalog digest is pinned as a current global value, and the superseded static repin with its 19 contracts and 83 artifacts census is historical evidence only.
